source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed electrical appliance safety checks

1. Start with the test records.
2.
completion:
3. Note the name, model, and serial number of the appliance being tested.
4. Describe the procedure used for testing, such as visual inspection, earth continuity testing, insulation resistance testing, leakage current testing, etc.
5. Record the date and time of the safety check.
6. State who performed the safety check and their credentials or qualifications.
7. Document the results of each test conducted, including specific measurements or observations.
8. Clearly state whether the appliance has passed or failed the safety check, with reasons for failure.
9. Include any warning signs observed, such as frayed cords, discolored or melted contacts, unusual noises, smells, etc.
10. If an appliance fails, specify what parts or systems are defective and provide recommendations for repair or disposal.
11. Take and attach photos of any defects or areas of concern.
12. Fill out any applicable checklists or forms accurately and completely.
13. Sign and date your documentation
